events.text: Case-insensitive filesystems are the default on macOS and Windows. Breakage that only shows up there usually means two paths that differ only by case. The ranker's top pick is a batch of Windows test changes; reading it first.

# INC-20151028-a3b357 — moby: Commit caused issues on systems with case-insensitive filesystems.

**SEV2** · **DIAGNOSED** · fired 2015-10-28T00:23:53+00:00 · diagnosed in 20.3s (4 tool calls)

## Summary

d5cd032a86 adds a top-level version/ directory, and the repository already has a VERSION file at its root. On a case-insensitive filesystem those are the same name, so checkouts and builds collide.

**Offending commit:** `d5cd032a86` · **Confidence:** 84% (high)

## Root-cause analysis

The symptom is specific to case-insensitive filesystems, which points at a path collision rather than a logic bug. Of the twelve suspects, only this one creates a new top-level path, and its name differs from the existing VERSION file only by case.

### Evidence

- d5cd032a86 adds version/version_lib.go and moves autogen/dockerversion to version
- VERSION already exists at the repository root
- 2af5034ce8 (the ranker's pick) only edits tests and an error message

### Candidates ruled out

- 2af5034ce8: Windows test changes; adds no new paths
